kept.claim: After taking the write lock, GetWebAssets does not re-check entryPointAssetsCache, so every goroutine that saw a nil cache during cold start re-reads and re-parses assets-manifest.json one after another instead of reusing the value the first writer stored.
kept.body:
## [RACE CONDITION] Double-checked locking is missing its second check

**Severity:** MEDIUM - on a cold cache, concurrent requests queue on a global mutex and each one repeats the manifest read and parse

### The Problem

```go
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.RLock()
ret := entryPointAssetsCache
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.RUnlock()

if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && ret != nil {
    return ret, nil
}
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()          // line 48
defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()  // line 49
// ... always reads the file and overwrites entryPointAssetsCache
```

Between `RUnlock` and `Lock`, another goroutine may already have filled the cache. The code does not check again after `Lock()`, so it reads the file anyway.

### Theory / Proof

This is the standard double-checked locking pattern. It only works if the condition is checked a second time while holding the exclusive lock. With `sync.RWMutex`, any number of readers can see `nil` at the same moment. Each of them then waits in `Lock()` and, once it gets the lock, runs `readWebAssetsFromFile` again: `os.Open`, a full JSON decode of the manifest, and rebuilding the integrity map. This happens on the first page loads after startup. Callers are `pkg/api/index.go:82` (every HTML index render), `pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:62` and `pkg/middleware/recovery.go:141`.

### What happens today vs. what will break

The results are still correct, because every writer stores an equivalent value. The cost is wasted work, and it is done one request at a time: N concurrent cold-start requests do the I/O N times in sequence while holding a process-wide lock.

### Research

The Go standard library provides `sync.Once` / `sync.OnceValues` (Go 1.21+) for lazy one-time initialisation. The Go memory model documentation recommends these over hand-written double-checked locking.

### Recommendation

At minimum, add the second check:

```go
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()
defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()
if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil {
    return entryPointAssetsCache, nil
}
```

Nothing re-checks the cache after Lock, so cold-start goroutines each reload in turn. Callers: index.go:82, frontendsettings.go:62, recovery.go:141. The missing-manifest scenario belongs to draft 2 and was removed from this body.

kept.claim: The exclusive lock is held across file I/O (and the CDN HTTP fetch path), so in Dev mode, or whenever the manifest fails to load, every index/frontend-settings/recovery request is serialized behind one global mutex.
kept.body:
## [OPTIMIZATION] File I/O happens while holding a global write lock

**Severity:** LOW - requests are serialized in Dev mode and when the manifest fails to load; in production with a healthy manifest this only affects startup

### The Problem

`defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()` keeps the exclusive lock held during `readWebAssetsFromFile` (open plus JSON decode). It is also held during `readWebAssetsFromCDN`, which sends an HTTP request with the caller's request context. That path is dead today (`cdn := ""`), but it is kept as a switch the team can turn on.

### Theory / Proof

When `cfg.Env == setting.Dev`, the fast path is always skipped, so every call takes `Lock()`. Concurrent calls from `index.go:82`, `frontendsettings.go:62` and `recovery.go:141` therefore run one at a time. Before this PR they ran concurrently (with a race). The same thing happens in production whenever the read fails, because a nil result is cached and the fast path never succeeds. If the CDN branch is enabled, one slow CDN response would block every page render for as long as the HTTP client takes.

### What happens today vs. what will break

With the default production setup and a valid manifest, the lock is taken once and nothing changes. Dev mode and failure mode lose concurrency. Turning on the CDN branch would make the global lock depend on network latency.

### Research

A common Go pattern is to do the expensive work without holding the lock and then publish the result with a short critical section, or to use `atomic.Pointer[T]` for the cached value.

### Recommendation

```go
var entryPointAssetsCache atomic.Pointer[dtos.EntryPointAssets]

func GetWebAssets(...) (*dtos.EntryPointAssets, error) {
    if cfg.Env != setting.Dev {
        if ret := entryPointAssetsCache.Load(); ret != nil {
            return ret, nil
        }
    }
    result, err := load(ctx, cfg, license) // no lock held
    entryPointAssetsCache.Store(result)
    return result, err
}
```

In production, use `sync.OnceValues` so the load runs only once.

In Dev mode the condition at line 45 is always false, so every call serializes. When the read fails, nil is cached at line 69 and every production call serializes too.

kept.claim: The PR fixes a data race but adds no concurrent test, so nothing under `go test -race` guards against a regression.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] No regression test for the data race being fixed

**Severity:** LOW - the fix has no test, so a later refactor could reintroduce the race without anyone noticing

### The Problem

`webassets_test.go` only tests `readWebAssetsFromFile` and `readWebAssetsFromCDN` (skipped). Nothing calls `GetWebAssets` from more than one goroutine, so the race detector never runs over the code this PR changes.

### Theory / Proof

The Go race detector only reports races on code paths that actually run. Without a test that calls `GetWebAssets` concurrently, CI's `-race` runs can neither confirm this fix nor catch a regression, for example someone removing the `RLock` on the fast path.

### What happens today vs. what will break

The fix is correct today. A future change such as the `TODO: get rid of global state` refactor could bring the race back without any test failing.

### Recommendation

```go
func TestGetWebAssetsConcurrent(t *testing.T) {
    cfg := setting.NewCfg()
    cfg.StaticRootPath = t.TempDir() // with build/assets-manifest.json copied from testdata
    var wg sync.WaitGroup
    for i := 0; i < 20; i++ {
        wg.Add(1)
        go func() {
            defer wg.Done()
            _, _ = GetWebAssets(context.Background(), cfg, &licensing.OSSLicensingService{})
        }()
    }
    wg.Wait()
}
```
